questions.q: Why is SSH on meridian-web-sg scoped to 203.0.113.0/24 instead of 0.0.0.0/0?
options: 0.0.0.0/0 would allow SSH login attempts from anywhere on the internet, not just Meridian's own office network
203.0.113.0/24 is the only CIDR block AWS allows for port 22
0.0.0.0/0 is reserved exclusively for HTTPS traffic
Scoping SSH has no real security benefit either way
questions.explain: Leaving SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0 is one of the most common security group mistakes — scoping it to a known office range cuts off the rest of the internet.

questions.q: What does --source-group sg-0meridianweb accomplish on the meridian-app-sg rule that a hardcoded CIDR block wouldn't?
options: It automatically covers any future instance added to the web tier's security group, with no IP range to maintain
It makes the rule run faster than a CIDR-based rule
It allows traffic from any AWS account, not just Meridian's
It disables the rule until manually activated
questions.explain: A source-group rule follows the group's membership automatically, so a new web instance is covered without editing the rule.

questions.q: Why does meridian-app1 get an IAM role and instance profile instead of an access key stored in its application config?
options: A role supplies temporary, auto-rotating credentials from instance metadata, with nothing stored that could leak
IAM roles are required for any EC2 instance launched in a private subnet
Access keys cannot be used by EC2 instances under any circumstances
Roles are faster to type than access keys
questions.explain: The whole point of an instance profile is eliminating a long-lived secret that could be copied, logged, or leaked.

questions.q: The CloudWatch alarm on meridian-web1 requires two consecutive 5-minute periods above 80% CPU before it fires. Why not fire on the first period?
options: Requiring a sustained threshold avoids triggering an alert on a single brief, harmless spike
CloudWatch alarms are technically incapable of firing on a single period
A single period of data is never collected by CloudWatch
80% is below the minimum threshold CloudWatch allows
questions.explain: evaluation-periods 2 means the condition has to hold across two consecutive periods, filtering out a one-off momentary spike.

questions.q: What's the difference in what an EBS snapshot and an AWS Budget each protect against?
options: A snapshot protects the data on a volume from loss; a budget protects against the account's spend getting away from you
They protect against exactly the same risk, just at different dollar thresholds
A snapshot protects spend; a budget protects data
Neither one actually protects anything — both are purely informational
questions.explain: An EBS snapshot is a backup of a volume's data; an AWS Budget is a spend-monitoring and alerting tool — different risks entirely.
